findings.body:
Any authenticated caller can set `body.accountId` and read that account’s full JSON. The new path never checks that the caller is support staff or otherwise allowed to access the target id — only `auth(req)` runs, then the client-supplied id is trusted.

Failure mode: an ordinary user sends `{"accountId":"<victim>"}` and receives the victim account record (PII, billing, internal fields — whatever `findUnique` returns).

Gate the override on an explicit staff/support authorization check from `caller`, and reject cross-account lookups for everyone else. Ordinary callers should keep resolving only `caller.accountId`.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change introduces a direct object reference on account lookup with no authorization gate.

## Narrative

`getAccount` previously scoped the query to `caller.accountId` from `auth(req)`, so each caller could only load their own account. The patch prefers `body.accountId` whenever it is present, with a comment that support staff tools will pass it explicitly. Nothing in the new path checks a staff role, permission, or allowlist before honoring that id.

Any authenticated client can therefore POST/PUT a body like `{"accountId": "<victim>"}` and receive that account’s JSON. That is a broken-authorization / IDOR failure on a sensitive record.

The TypeScript annotation on `id` also does not validate at runtime: a non-string `accountId` would flow into `findUnique` unchanged. Secondary to the authz gap, but worth hardening when the staff path is implemented correctly.

## Recommended fix direction

Before using a client-supplied id, require an explicit staff/support authorization decision from `caller` (role claim, capability flag, or equivalent). Reject the request when a non-staff caller supplies `accountId` other than their own. Keep the default `caller.accountId` path for ordinary users.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The head path sets `id` from `body.accountId ?? caller.accountId` after only `auth(req)`, with no staff/ownership check, then returns `findUnique` JSON—so any authenticated caller can read another account. Base only used `caller.accountId`, so this is a real IDOR regression.
